title: Dominic and the Salt
premise: Hazel Zhou, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who has gone silent, keeps the ledgers of the Salt Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed luck, second chances. When the crown declares a hunt for anyone carrying the gift of soul-craft, Hazel learns their own name sits at the top of the list, entered there years ago in their dead mother's handwriting. The only way to erase it is to steal back a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain: the soul of Wren, the guild's youngest runner and the one person Hazel swore to protect. The theft forces Hazel to choose between loyalty to the guild that raised them and the truth that the silent god never left—it has been devouring its sworn servants one ledger at a time. In the end, Hazel burns the ledgers, breaks their oath, and pays the god's price themselves so Wren can walk free into a winter that finally ends.
about_author: Lior Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging debt records from defunct merchant houses before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep accounts with things that cannot be repaid.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unpaid Things
chapters.summary: Hazel audits the Salt Guild's winter inventory, cataloging impossible goods while hiding their own gift from the other mercenaries. A routine entry reveals a page torn from the oldest ledger—the year of their mother's death. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced competence.

chapters.title: What the Bell Ringer Knew
chapters.summary: Wren, the guild's youngest runner, delivers a package to a client who recognizes the gift in her and lets her live—for now. She reports back to Hazel, lying about what she saw. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the first crack in the guild's invisibility.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Ashgate
chapters.summary: The crown posts the hunt decree; soldiers burn a hedge-witch in the square as an example. The guild master orders everyone to scatter and go dark. Hazel notices their own name is already on the crown's list—dated eleven years ago. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the past arriving all at once.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Mother
chapters.summary: Hazel deciphers their mother's entries and finds a transaction: a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain, payment deferred, collateral named—Hazel themselves. POV: Hazel, with flashback fragments. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Guild Splits
chapters.summary: The guild votes on whether to surrender Wren to buy safety. Hazel argues against; the vote fails. That night someone marks Hazel's door with the god's old sigil. POV: Brannick, a rival mercenary. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to rot.

chapters.title: Salt Roads South
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren flee toward the mountain ahead of the hunters, trading favors with smugglers who remember Hazel's mother. Wren confesses she knows she was sold—that she remembers the court. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: trust built on shared damage.

chapters.title: The Silent God Speaks Once
chapters.summary: At a ruined shrine, the god stirs for the first time in years, showing Hazel a vision of servants kneeling in the dark, being consumed. It offers a bargain if Hazel comes alone. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: terror wearing the face of hope.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Icefield
chapters.summary: Crown hunters corner them on the frozen pass. Hazel uses the gift openly for the first time, unraveling a hunter's borrowed luck—and feels the god drinking the act. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: power that costs more than it gives.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Debts
chapters.summary: They shelter with a tollkeeper who buys memories. Wren sells a happy childhood memory to pay passage, choosing which self to lose. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the price of survival made intimate and small.

chapters.title: Brannick Finds Them
chapters.summary: Brannick catches up, ostensibly to warn them: the guild master sold Wren's location to the crown to save the rest. He offers Hazel a place among the deserters. POV: Brannick. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Hazel enters the under-mountain court through a debtor's door, posing as a collector come to audit old accounts. The court's beauty is a ledger itself—everything owed, nothing owned. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: awe laced with horror.

chapters.title: Audience with the Under-Crown
chapters.summary: The court's ruler shows Hazel the original contract: their mother sold Wren's soul to buy Hazel's erasure from the hunt list. Every kindness Hazel remembered is re-priced. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: identity collapsing under the true cost of survival.

chapters.title: Wren in the Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Interlude below: Wren, captured en route, waits in the vault where souls are filed. She meets other stored souls and begins picking the vault's lock with a stolen memory-shard. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: defiance in captivity.

chapters.title: The Counter-Offer
chapters.summary: The under-crown offers Hazel a trade: take Wren's place, or bring the god something worth more than a soul. Hazel pretends to negotiate while memorizing the vault's layout. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: cold clarity inside desperation.

chapters.title: What Brannick Owes
chapters.summary: Brannick arrives to sell out Hazel's plan and instead finds his own name in the court's books—he was collateral all along. He chooses, badly and bravely, to hold the door. POV: Brannick. Emotional beat: redemption bought too late to enjoy.

chapters.title: The Theft of Wren
chapters.summary: Hazel reaches the vault as alarms rise; Wren has already freed half the shelves. Together they pull her name from the ledger—but removing it unravels the court's bindings, and everything stored starts waking. POV: alternating Hazel/Wren. Emotional beat: triumph that triggers catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Court Wakes
chapters.summary: Escaping through a collapsing under-mountain, they release souls as they run, including the god's devoured servants, whose memories flood into Hazel. They learn the god's full nature. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: unbearable knowledge as fuel.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Above ground, the god manifests fully, demanding payment for the stolen soul and the broken contract. Hazel offers the only thing it wants: the last living servant who can still swear oaths—themselves. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Instead of swearing anew, Hazel burns the mother's contract page and renounces the god aloud, using the released servants' memories as leverage. The god, starved of worshippers, shrinks to something small enough to refuse. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: liberation through refusal.

chapters.title: Reckoning at the Guild Hall
chapters.summary: Hazel returns to confront the guild master, presenting the ledgers as evidence before the assembled members. The guild dissolves rather than face the crown; some follow Hazel, most scatter. Brannick's body comes home. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: justice without satisfaction.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Turns
chapters.summary: Deep winter breaks early over the valley—an old sign that the mountain's debts are settled. Hazel and Wren bury the ledgers' ashes and plant salt-tolerant flowers over them. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Salt
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Hazel takes the name Dominic, their mother's first choice for them, and opens a small honest shop that trades only in possible things. Wren runs deliveries. On the shelf, a single blank ledger waits. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, future unwritten.
